meta.audience: The multitude at the temple in Bountiful
meta.location: The temple in the land Bountiful
meta.date: AD 34, late in the thirty-fourth year
meta.unit: The destruction and the visit (3 Nephi 8–11)
principles: A voice heard three times before it is understood
A witness taken one by one
A doctrine defined by what may not be added to it

world_behind.title: Less than a year had passed
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 8:5 dates the storm to the fourth day of the first month of the thirty and fourth year, and 3 Nephi 10:18 places this visit in the ending of that same year. The people conversing in verse 1 are standing on ground that was rearranged inside the last twelve months.

world_behind.title: The size of the crowd is given six chapters later
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 17:25 numbers the multitude at about two thousand and five hundred souls, men, women and children. This chapter never counts them, and that figure is what turns verse 15 into a procession of hours.

world_behind.title: Bountiful is the northern frontier
world_behind.text: Alma 22:29 to 33 puts the land Bountiful at the top of Nephite territory, a day and a half's journey wide from the east sea to the west and bordering the land Desolation across the narrow neck. The gathering happens at the edge of the settled country rather than at its center.

world_behind.title: The old center was gone
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 9:3 has the great city Zarahemla burned with fire, and the voice in that chapter names sixteen cities destroyed. The place the record had used as its capital since the days of Mosiah no longer existed when this crowd assembled.

world_behind.title: Baptism was already being practised, and already disputed
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 7:25 has Nephi ordaining men to the ministry of baptism, and 7:26 reports many baptized in that same year. Verse 28 adds that there had hitherto been disputations about it. The dictated words in verse 25 settle the manner and the authority of something the people had been doing and arguing over for at least a year.

world_behind.title: What survives is a selection made under restriction
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 26:6 says this book cannot contain a hundredth part of what Jesus taught, and 26:11 says Mormon was forbidden to write what he had begun to write. These chapters are not a transcript, and the record says so itself.

words.text: Talking together. Both of the record's uses are in this chapter, at verses 2 and 3, and the King James Bible has neither. The crowd is mid-conversation when the voice comes.
Treated at Alma 40:23, of the body restored to its proper frame. The record uses the word ten times. Verse 3 says no part of their frame escaped the quaking.
Marks left by pressure. Verses 14 and 15 hold both uses the record has, with none in the King James Bible. John 20:25 uses "print" in the singular of the same marks.
Agreement, in the phrase "with one accord." The record uses it three times and the King James Bible sixteen, mostly in Acts. Verse 16 has a whole multitude crying out together.
Arguments, contentions over points. It appears eleven times in the record, and the King James Bible once. Four uses cluster around this command and its outcome in 4 Nephi 1:2.
To put wholly under. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, in the instruction on how baptism is performed.

phrases.term: It was not a harsh voice, neither was it a loud voice... it did pierce them to the very soul
phrases.text: The voice described by what it was not. Helaman 5:30 had described another voice the same way and used the same word for piercing.

phrases.term: The third time they did understand the voice which they heard
phrases.text: Understanding arrives on the third hearing, after they opened their ears and looked toward the sound. The change is in the listeners.

phrases.term: Behold my Beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased... hear ye him
phrases.text: The Father's only words in the chapter. Matthew 17:5 gives the same sentence on the mount, including the final command.

phrases.term: They thought it was an angel that had appeared unto them
phrases.text: The crowd's first reading of what they saw. The record lets the mistake stand for two verses.

phrases.term: I have drunk out of that bitter cup which the Father hath given me
phrases.text: His first description of himself after the name. What he offers as identification is what he suffered.

phrases.term: Going forth one by one until they had all gone forth
phrases.text: The witness taken individually. Verse 15 says they saw with their eyes, felt with their hands, knew of a surety, and bore record.

phrases.term: Nephi arose and went forth, and bowed himself before the Lord and did kiss his feet
phrases.text: The one personal action reported in the chapter. He is then told to stand up.

phrases.term: On this wise shall ye baptize; and there shall be no disputations among you
phrases.text: The authority and the prohibition given in one sentence. The manner is specified so the manner cannot be argued about.

phrases.term: He that hath the spirit of contention is not of me
phrases.text: The sharpest sentence in the chapter. Verse 29 names the devil as the father of contention and describes what he stirs up.

phrases.term: Ye must repent, and become as a little child
phrases.text: Stated twice, in verses 37 and 38, with the two clauses reversed. The repetition is exact except for the order.

phrases.term: Whoso shall declare more or less than this, and establish it for my doctrine, the same cometh of evil
phrases.text: The boundary drawn in both directions. Adding and subtracting are named as the same error.

verses.label: v. 3–6
verses.title: Two failures of hearing before the third attempt
verses.text: The record does not report a voice that was simply understood. It reports two misses and then a change in the listeners: "they heard a voice as if it came out of heaven; and they cast their eyes round about, for they understood not the voice which they heard"; "again they heard the voice, and they understood it not"; and then "the third time they did hear the voice, and did open their ears to hear it; and their eyes were towards the sound thereof." What changes between the second attempt and the third is described as an act of the audience, opening the ears and looking toward the sound, rather than a change in the voice.

verses.label: v. 14–15
verses.title: A verification performed by everyone, one at a time
verses.text: The invitation is plural and specific about the evidence: "Arise and come forth unto me, that ye may thrust your hands into my side, and also that ye may feel the prints of the nails in my hands and in my feet, that ye may know that I am the God of Israel." The report insists on the count: "going forth one by one until they had all gone forth, and did see with their eyes and did feel with their hands, and did know of a surety and did bear record." John 20:27 gives the same invitation to a single man. Here the record has a multitude do it in series and makes the seriality part of the account.

verses.label: v. 28
verses.title: A prohibition that names the dispute it is ending
verses.text: The instruction against contention is not general: "there shall be no disputations among you, as there have hitherto been; neither shall there be disputations among you concerning the points of my doctrine, as there have hitherto been." The clause as there have hitherto been appears twice, and the record has already reported the dispute it refers to. At 3 Ne. 1:24–25 a few began to preach "that it was no more expedient to observe the law of Moses," and were corrected. The prohibition points back at a specific quarrel rather than at an attitude.

verses.label: v. 37–38
verses.title: The same three items, in two different orders
verses.text: The record gives the requirement twice in consecutive verses and swaps the middle terms: "ye must repent, and become as a little child, and be baptized in my name, or ye can in nowise receive these things"; then "ye must repent, and be baptized in my name, and become as a little child, or ye can in nowise inherit the kingdom of God." Repentance stays first in both. The other two exchange places, and the consequence clause changes as well, from receiving to inheriting.

verses.label: v. 40
verses.title: A limit set in both directions at once
verses.text: The boundary on the doctrine forbids addition and subtraction in the same clause: "whoso shall declare more or less than this, and establish it for my doctrine, the same cometh of evil, and is not built upon my rock." Most warnings of this kind guard against one error. This one names both, and it applies the same verdict to each, so a teacher who says too little is placed in the same category as one who says too much.

chapter.title: The failure to understand is reported twice
chapter.text: Verses 3 and 4 have them missing it. The record spends four verses on the hearing before anything is heard.

chapter.title: The voice is quiet
chapter.text: Verse 3 rules out harshness and loudness and then describes an effect that reaches the center of the body. Helaman 5:30 had already established the pattern.

chapter.title: They guess wrong first
chapter.text: Verse 8 has them concluding it was an angel. Their reverence and their error are reported together.

chapter.title: He identifies himself by the cup
chapter.text: Verse 11 gives the name and then the suffering. The credential offered is what he went through.

chapter.title: The witness is not taken as a crowd
chapter.text: Verse 15 insists on one by one until all had gone forth. A multitude of individual witnesses is what the chapter produces.

chapter.title: The manner of baptism is dictated to remove the argument
chapter.text: Verses 22 and 28 both attach the prohibition on disputations to the instruction. Precision here is given as the cure for contention.

chapter.title: Contention is given a father
chapter.text: Verse 29 assigns it a source rather than treating it as a temperament. 4 Nephi 1:2 will report a generation without it.

chapter.title: The doctrine is bounded on both sides
chapter.text: Verse 40 names declaring more and declaring less as the same failure. The rock is defined by its edges.

applications.title: Listen again before concluding you did not hear
applications.text: They got it on the third try, and the record says twice that they "understood not the voice which they heard." Nothing changed except the attention they gave it. When something did not land, the first move is another pass, not a verdict.

applications.title: Open your ears and look up
applications.text: The verse names two physical actions that preceded understanding, opening the ears and casting the eyes upward. Some of what looks like a comprehension problem is a posture problem, and the cheapest thing to change is what you are doing with your body while you listen.

applications.title: Let people come one at a time
applications.text: The witness was taken individually, "one by one," from a crowd of twenty-five hundred. When you want people to be sure of something, build the version that survives being done singly.

applications.title: Specify the method to end the argument
applications.text: The words and the manner of baptism are given exactly, and verse 28 gives the reason: "there shall be no disputations among you concerning the points of my doctrine." When a recurring quarrel is about procedure, publishing the procedure is the fix.

applications.title: Treat contention as the thing itself, not the symptom
applications.text: "He that hath the spirit of contention is not of me," and then, in case the point is missed, "this is my doctrine, that such things should be done away." The instruction is not to win the argument differently. It is to stop having it.

applications.title: Say it twice with the terms reversed
applications.text: Repent and become as a little child and be baptized; then repent and be baptized and become as a little child. Two orderings of one instruction, one verse apart. When something matters, say it again in a form that cannot be mistaken for the first.

applications.title: Watch for adding as well as subtracting
applications.text: More or less than the doctrine both fail the test. The temptation to improve on an instruction is as real as the temptation to trim it, and only one of them feels like disobedience.

questions.text: What have I heard without understanding?
What have I misidentified because I had no category for it?
If I had to identify myself by what I have borne, what would I say?
What do I know of a surety, and how did I come to know it?
What would I do if I were called out of the crowd by name?
Where am I carrying a spirit of contention?
What have I added to the doctrine, or taken from it?
